text: The eleven slides of version 5 are kept word for word as approved, and the new slides 13 to 22 are the answer of this version: where version 5 says 'the Workbench', 'the Workbench module' or names a module, the new slide names the owning service of the Microservice Ownership Map v1.
why: Rule 1 and Template and Rules R8.2 never edit an existing file or an approved statement, while the realignment must still give every flow an owner; R1 U2 applies the same reading to Epic 1 work.
read: A reader sees version 5 as issued on slides 3 to 12 and finds the owner of each flow on the new slides, without having to compare two decks.
applied_in: Information Flow v6, read-me slide 2, change table slide 13 and the notes of slides 14 to 22
impact: The deck holds two readings of the same flow in one file; the new slides are the authoritative owner statement for the build.

text: Version 6 is issued in Draft. No approval is recorded for this version, and the run continues without a human verification stop.
why: The run is a realignment with no approval step (R1 U8) and the source deck carries no approval record; the alternative, waiting, would stop the work package.
read: A reader knows the deck may change after review and does not treat it as approved for build.
applied_in: Information Flow v6, read-me slide 2, status line
impact: None on content; the status line changes when approval is recorded.

text: The title slide of version 5 stays slide 1 and the read-me slide of this version, which carries the R8.1 header lines, is slide 2. The page number of every source slide follows its new position, so slides 2 to 11 of version 5 are numbered 3 to 12 here.
why: Template and Rules R8.1 puts the two header lines at the start and R8.2 forbids removing a slide of the source; a new first slide would push the title slide away, while an unnumbered read-me slide keeps every source slide in order.
read: The deck opens on its title, the header is on the first slide after it, and no page number repeats or skips.
applied_in: Information Flow v6, slides 1 and 2, and the page number of every slide
impact: The page numbers of the source slides are one higher than in version 5; the slide text is unchanged.

text: gateway-bff, the Redis session and the App Gateway route are owned by the platform edge epic RWB-PLT-EDGE with the platform team, and the composite route contract is RWB-PLT-N001-CON.
why: The Ownership Map v1 has no row for the edge, and the deck cannot name an owner without one; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-19 and R5.7 rule 6 give the edge a platform contract story.
read: Every screen flow of the deck has an owner: the edge is platform work, the owning service answers behind it, and no service code is invented for it.
applied_in: Information Flow v6, shared platform slide 20, row 'gateway-bff and Redis'
impact: The edge stories carry the ownership until a row is added to the Ownership Map; no service contract changes.

text: O05 (decisions and outcomes to COLLINS for model learning) has no replacement path after the data lake is removed and is recorded as open, not invented. P9 rwb-reporting's event read model is the nearest source of the same data.
why: ADR-018 and DP-17 remove the lake, and no source names an interface to COLLINS; inventing one would put an unapproved interface on an approved deck.
read: A reader knows O04 is answered by P9 and O05 is not answered at all, and the model owner has to decide.
applied_in: Information Flow v6, change table slide 13, row O04 and O05; open points slide 22
impact: COLLINS model learning has no feed at wave 1; the reporting read model is unaffected.

text: ace_batch_run is read through recovery.v_ace_batch_status by P1 rwb-source-data only, and P1 raises AceDataLate and runs the batch check.
why: ADR-010 and DP-05 allow one read path, the 30 views, and P1 is their only reader; the view exists in the physical schema.
read: The fallback rows of the deck name one reader and one view, and the ACE table name stays only as the source's wording.
applied_in: Information Flow v6, fallback slide 21, rows 'ACE refuses a feed' and 'An ACE source is late'
impact: No service may query ace_batch_run directly; the P1 contract has to expose the business date and the staleness flag.

text: The interaction ledger stays with P1 rwb-source-data (R3 default ruling, DP-18), and its readers are served through the P1 contract; the deck names no reader because no source does.
why: R3 gives the ledger to P1 and DP-18 confirms it; a reader list would be invented and would bind three services to an interface that is not designed yet.
read: The ledger has one owner and one read path; the reader list is a P1 contract item before the wave 1 freeze.
applied_in: Information Flow v6, platform services slide 14, row P1, and open points slide 22
impact: P6, P3 and S2 stories that need contact history depend on the P1 contract story, not on a new ledger service.

text: A partner result is recorded by S9 rwb-partner, which publishes PartnerResultSubmitted; the dated DP06 to DP08 copies stay with P1 as read-only data products built from the S9 events.
why: Architecture v5 slide 17 gives rwb-partner the results and the event, and the Ownership Map ruling keeps only the dated copies with P1.
read: One service records a court date, an enforcement step, an appraisal report or a sale result, and the data products follow it.
applied_in: Information Flow v6, change table slide 13, row I13 and O06; stage services slide 15, row S9
impact: S4 and S5 consume PartnerResultSubmitted from S9 rather than reading a P1 copy.

text: P4 rwb-access owns roles, scope, masking policy and the DoA table; P1 rwb-source-data reads recovery.v_ace_iam_group and serves it through its contract; sign-in and group-to-role stay with ACE Common.
why: ADR-010 allows only P1 to read the views, and Architecture v5 slide 14 gives P4 the roles as data and ACE Common the group-to-role step.
read: The I16 row of the deck has three named parties and no fourth reading of the same data.
applied_in: Information Flow v6, change table slide 13, row I16; platform services slide 14, row P4
impact: P4 needs the P1 contract for group data and keeps its own access log; no service reads iam_group directly.

text: P6 rwb-comms makes the call to the ACE Common notification path for SMS and LINE, and builds its own dispatch only if the ACE team confirms that no bank-wide service exists; DL30 stays open.
why: Architecture v5 gives rwb-comms the notification call in its OUT contract and keeps the bank-wide service question open; picking the call is the only way to give O03 an owner.
read: O03 has an owner and a path, and the open question in the gaps table is not closed by the deck.
applied_in: Information Flow v6, change table slide 13, row O03; open points slide 22
impact: P6 stories carry the notification integration until DL30 closes; no other service calls NSS or LINE OA.

text: For the WIN registered-mail file, P6 rwb-comms owns the notice and the JOB-10 Schedule, and P2 rwb-integration owns the transport and the retry, publishing FileDelivered or FileFailed to P6.
why: Architecture v5 writes the JOB-10 owner as 'rwb-comms + integration' and gives P2 the file transport; splitting the accountabilities is the only reading with one owner per step.
read: A failed acknowledgement has one service to retry and one service to raise the task from.
applied_in: Information Flow v6, change table slide 13, row O02; fallback slide 21, last row; shared platform slide 20, row Airflow
impact: The P6 and P2 contract tests cover the file hand-off; the Airflow window is owned by the bank scheduler.

text: Two kinds of Kafka traffic are described side by side: the ACE PII logging topics, unchanged, and the 19 business topics rwb.<short>.events.v1 plus the shared rwb.decision-record.v1 added by ADR-015.
why: Version 5 names only the PII use, and ADR-015 adds business events; a reader needs both to size partitions, ACLs and retention.
read: The change table gives the business topics and keeps the PII topics as they are, with different ACLs and no personal data on the business topics.
applied_in: Information Flow v6, change table slide 13, row on Kafka; event slides 16 and 17
impact: The Kafka platform creates 20 new topics for Recovery and leaves the PII topics untouched.

text: Version 5 carries no release date. The document dates of 15 November 2026 (title slide) and 22 November 2026 (this version) are kept as issued and read as tentative under R1 U7 and DL48.
why: Rule 10 and R1 U7 forbid changing a date or raising one as a gap, and the deck is a design document with no release schedule of its own.
read: No date is lost and no new date is invented; the wave of each flow comes from the owning service.
applied_in: Information Flow v6, title slide 1 and read-me slide 2
impact: None; the deck stays aligned with the programme calendar.

text: Every owner in the deck is a service code P1 to P10 or S1 to S9 of the Microservice Ownership Map v1, a platform epic (RWB-PLT-*), or a party outside the 19 services; no owner is a team type, a person or a story master.
why: R1 U3 forbids names of people, the Ownership Map is the only owner source for this run, and R-PREC puts Architecture v5 above the story masters.
read: Each flow has one accountable service and the parties outside the 19 services are named as such.
impact: Story ownership follows the same codes, so the deck and the story files agree.

text: The wave of a flow is the wave of the service that owns it, as Rules R4 and Architecture v5 slide 38 give it: wave 1 for P1 to P7, P9 and P10; wave 2 for P8, S2, S5 and S8; wave 3 for S1, S3, S4 and S6; wave 4 for S7 and S9.
why: The source deck carries no wave and the realignment needs one per flow; the service waves are already decided in two sources that agree.
read: A reader can see when a flow exists: an event between two services starts when the later of the two is built.
applied_in: Information Flow v6, platform services slide 14 and stage services slide 15, wave column
impact: Integration tests of a flow wait for the later service's wave; nothing is built earlier than its epic.

text: The in and out columns of the two ownership slides are transcribed from the Architecture v5 service contracts (slides 14 to 20) and the Ownership Map v1; no interface, table, event or topic is added.
why: R-PREC puts the Architecture v5 catalogue first, and a transcription keeps the deck consistent with the Service Catalog and the Service Contract Catalog.
read: The decks and the catalogues carry the same interfaces, so a build team can work from either.
applied_in: Information Flow v6, platform services slide 14 and stage services slide 15
impact: Any later change to a contract has to be made in Architecture v5 and the two catalogues first.
